title: AlphaMemo: Structured Search-Process Memory for Self-Evolving Alpha Mining Agents

title: Measuring Strategy-Decay Risk: Minimum Regime Performance and the Durability of Systematic Investing
strategy: Introduces Minimum Regime Performance (MRP) -- the lowest realized risk-adjusted return of a strategy across historical market regimes -- as a robustness/durability metric to complement (and sometimes contradict) standard full-sample Sharpe ratio for systematic factor strategies.
universe_period: A broad universe of established factor strategies (specific factors not fully captured)

notes: Key finding: strategies with higher long-run Sharpe ratios do not always have higher MRP -- i.e., some high-average-Sharpe factors are fragile in specific regimes. Directly useful methodology for stress-testing any of the momentum/value/quality signals in this list against a 2026 AI-mega-cap-concentration regime. Code is public on GitHub.

title: CLQT: A Closed-Loop, Cost-Aware, Strategy-Consistent Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Portfolio-Management Agents

title: Option-Implied Signals and Crash Risk: Predictability and Machine-Learning Evidence from U.S. Equity Options, 2015-2026
strategy: Constructs a daily firm-level panel of six option-implied signals (volatility smirk, IV spread, risk-neutral skewness proxy, term-structure slope, put-call volume/OI ratios) and tests their next-month return and crash-risk predictability across three macro regimes (2015-2019 low-vol, 2020-2022 high-vol, 2023-2026 AI/mega-cap), comparing linear regressions to XGBoost.

No transaction costs modeled.

title: Executable Arbitrage and Market Efficiency in Prediction Markets
strategy: Uses high-resolution order-book snapshots on prediction markets (e.g., Polymarket) to detect arbitrage opportunities in real time, then measures how persistent and how actually executable (against real liquidity) those opportunities are, distinguishing theoretical from tradeable mispricing.

Not directly relevant to a US tech-equity long/short book but included per the research brief's scope.

title: Arbitrage Analysis in Polymarket NBA Markets

title: Semantic Non-Fungibility and Violations of the Law of One Price in Prediction Markets
strategy: Documents cross-platform (e.g., Polymarket vs. Kalshi) violations of the law of one price for economically equivalent (but not identically worded/structured) prediction-market contracts, attributing fragmentation to structural factors like differing resolution rules and institutional segmentation rather than pure inefficiency.
how_to_recreate: Requires matched-contract price data across platforms; identify semantically-equivalent contracts with different resolution language, measure price divergence, test whether the divergence is arbitrageable given platform-specific settlement risk and withdrawal/transfer frictions.
notes: Finding that fragmentation is 'structural rather than incidental' implies apparent cross-platform arbitrage may not be safely executable due to resolution-rule risk, not just execution cost.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Diversified Portfolio Management Across Global Equity Markets
strategy: DRL framework for portfolio allocation across global equity markets, optimizing a differential Sharpe ratio reward net of transaction costs; a related PPO variant is also used for options-hedging tasks comparable to Black-Scholes delta hedging.

notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass -- notable as one of the few papers blending LLM text signals directly into a stat-arb/pairs framework.

title: AlphaAgent: LLM-Driven Alpha Mining with Regularized Exploration to Counteract Alpha Decay
authors: Ziyi Tang, Zechuan Chen, Jiarui Yang, Jiayao Mai, Yongsen Zheng, Keze Wang, Jinrui Chen, Liang Lin
strategy: LLM-agent-driven formulaic alpha search with three regularizers -- AST-based originality/similarity penalty vs. known factors, LLM-scored hypothesis-factor semantic alignment, and AST-based complexity control -- intended to produce decay-resistant alphas rather than overfit/curve-fit factors.
universe_period: CSI 500 (China) and S&P 500 (US), 4-year test spanning bull and bear regimes
how_to_recreate: Requires daily price/fundamental data for the target universe and an LLM to propose/evaluate candidate alpha formulas; iterate a generate-evaluate-regularize loop (originality, alignment, complexity) and backtest each surviving formula. Feasible with Massive-style daily data plus an LLM API, but requires building the regularization/search harness.

title: R&D-Agent-Quant (RD-Agent(Q)): A Multi-Agent Framework for Data-Centric Factors and Model Joint Optimization

notes: Reports RD-Agent(Q) achieves up to 2x the annualized return of classical factor libraries using 70% fewer factors, at very low compute cost (all experiments reportedly under $10). Code and framework are public, making this one of the more directly reproducible papers in this list -- but results are on Qlib's standard market setups, and the ARR is a backtest IC-driven metric, not a live P&L.

title: Cryptocurrency as an Investable Asset Class: Coming of Age
authors: Nicola Borri, Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski, Xi Wu
strategy: Extends the crypto three-factor model (market, size, momentum) with a value factor to form a four-factor (C-4) model; organizes crypto empirical asset-pricing regularities into seven stylized facts and argues crypto risk-adjusted performance is now broadly comparable to traditional asset classes.
universe_period: Broad cryptocurrency universe, updated through the mid-2020s
how_to_recreate: Requires daily crypto price/volume/on-chain data; add a value factor (e.g., based on network-value-to-transactions or a price-to-fundamental-usage ratio) to the existing C-3 factors, re-test spanning of characteristic-sorted portfolios.

notes: Consistent with equity-momentum literature (volatility-managed momentum reduces crash risk); crypto momentum crashes are noted elsewhere to differ structurally from equity momentum crashes (crypto lacks the same extended-crash pattern per one 2025 study).

title: The Many Facets of Stock Momentum: Distinguishing Factor and Stock Components
strategy: Decomposes stock momentum into a factor-momentum component and a residual stock-specific component internationally, testing whether Ehsani-Linnainmaa's 'factor momentum explains stock momentum' finding holds outside the US.
how_to_recreate: Requires international factor-return panels plus stock-level momentum signals; decompose stock momentum returns into factor-momentum-explained and residual components via spanning regressions across countries.
notes: Finds factor momentum exists internationally but fails to fully explain price or industry momentum outside specific markets -- a useful counterweight to the pure 'factor momentum subsumes stock momentum' narrative for a global/non-US-only interpretation.

title: Not All Factors Crowd Equally: Modeling, Measuring, and Trading on Alpha Decay
strategy: Proposed a hyperbolic alpha-decay model (alpha(t) = K/(1+lambda*t)) fit to eight Fama-French factors, and tested a crowding-based factor-selection strategy meant to trade on differential decay/crowding across factors.
reported_sharpe: crowding-based factor-selection Sharpe of 0.22 vs. 0.39 for a plain factor-momentum benchmark; out-of-sample alpha of 0.30 vs. 0.15 reported in one specification; momentum showed 0.38x the crash probability of a 1.7-1.8x higher crash probability for crowded reversal strategies
how_to_recreate: Requires the eight Fama-French factor series (public data); fit hyperbolic/linear/exponential decay curves to each factor's rolling Sharpe or alpha over time, build a crowding proxy, and test whether avoiding/favoring crowded factors improves risk-adjusted return.
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this paper was WITHDRAWN by the author, who states 'empirical validation in Sections 5-7 is insufficient to support global applicability claims.' The crowding-based strategy is explicitly reported to underperform (Sharpe 0.22) the simple factor-momentum benchmark (0.39), i.e., a negative result for the proposed approach -- do not use the specific numbers here as validated findings; included mainly as a cautionary data point on factor crowding/decay methodology.

title: Does Overnight News Explain Overnight Returns?
authors: Paul Glasserman, Kriste Krstovski, Paul Laliberte, Harry Mamaysky
strategy: Applies supervised topic modeling to 2.4 million news articles to identify which news topics are associated with abnormal overnight (close-to-open) versus intraday (open-to-close) returns, and uses topic prevalence/response differences to forecast which stocks will do well overnight and poorly intraday (or vice versa).
universe_period: US equities, roughly 30-year sample of news and returns
how_to_recreate: Requires a large historical news corpus plus split overnight/intraday return series. Fit supervised topic models (e.g., seeded LDA or an LLM-based topic classifier) to link topics to return components, then form a daily long-short overnight-return-forecast portfolio entering near the close and exiting at the next open.
notes: Confirms and extends a long literature (Lou-Polk-Skouras 'Tug of War', NY Fed 'Overnight Drift') documenting that most US equity index gains accrue overnight rather than intraday; a Massive-style news+price feed could reproduce the topic-modeling approach, though exact performance figures were not retrievable from the abstract alone.

title: StockBench: Can LLM Agents Trade Stocks Profitably in Real-World Markets?
authors: Yanxu Chen, Zijun Yao, Yantao Liu, Amy Xin, Jin Ye, Jianing Yu, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
strategy: Contamination-free, continuously-updated multi-stock trading benchmark: LLM agents receive daily prices, fundamentals and news and must issue sequential buy/sell/hold decisions over a multi-month window; evaluated via cumulative return, max drawdown and Sortino ratio against a buy-and-hold baseline.
universe_period: Multi-stock, multi-month live/continuously-updated window (state-of-the-art proprietary models GPT-5/Claude-4 and open models Qwen3/Kimi-K2/GLM-4.5 tested)
reported_return: buy-and-hold baseline achieves a modest 0.4% return over the test window (max drawdown -15.2%, Sortino 0.0155); several LLM agents deliver returns above 2%
how_to_recreate: Requires daily prices, fundamentals and news for a stock universe, plus an LLM agent loop that ingests this daily and outputs buy/sell/hold; compute cumulative return, max drawdown, Sortino vs. buy-and-hold. This is essentially a template directly reproducible with a Massive-style data feed and any LLM API.
notes: Key finding: most LLM agents struggle to beat simple buy-and-hold, and static financial-knowledge benchmark performance does not translate into trading skill -- an important sobering data point against over-trusting LLM-agent trading claims elsewhere in this list. Test-period market conditions (a period with a low 0.4% buy-and-hold return) likely favored active agents mechanically; results may not generalize to strongly trending markets.

title: When Agents Trade: Live Multi-Market Trading Benchmark for LLM Agents (Agent Market Arena)
strategy: Lifelong, real-time multi-market benchmark for LLM trading agents; implements four agent architectures (InvestorAgent, TradeAgent, HedgeFundAgent, DeepFundAgent with memory) tested across five LLM backbones (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, Claude-3.5-haiku, Claude-sonnet-4, Gemini-2.0-flash) live on crypto and stock markets.

how_to_recreate: Requires live/near-live price, fundamentals and news feeds for the target markets, plus an implementation of the four agent archetypes (varying risk style and memory use) run against multiple LLM backbones; track live cumulative return per agent-model pair.
notes: Key finding: agent architecture (not the underlying LLM) is the primary driver of performance differences -- risk-taking vs. conservative agent design matters more than swapping GPT-4o for Claude or Gemini. A single-stock 40.83% TSLA return over an unspecified short live window is a striking but low-sample-size result; do not extrapolate to a diversified book.

title: LiveTradeBench: Seeking Real-World Alpha with Large Language Models
strategy: A live (real-time, forward-testing) benchmark for evaluating whether LLM-based trading strategies can generate genuine, non-backtested alpha, addressing the look-ahead/contamination concerns endemic to backtested LLM trading papers.

notes: Forward/live testing is the most credible way to sidestep LLM training-data-cutoff look-ahead risk that plagues most other LLM-signal papers in this list; worth prioritizing this design pattern (paper trading forward, not backtesting on pre-cutoff historical news) when evaluating any LLM-based signal for the target book.

title: FinDPO: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Preference Optimization of LLMs
authors: Giorgos Iacovides, Wuyang Zhou, Danilo Mandic

Convert model logits to a continuous score, rank stocks daily, form long-short portfolio, apply ~5bps assumed transaction costs. DPO fine-tuning requires ML infra beyond a pure signals pipeline.
notes: Reported 5bps costs are a modeling assumption, not measured live costs; 67%/Sharpe 2.0 is a backtest figure and should be treated as an upper bound given typical alpha decay for sentiment strategies once crowded.

how_to_recreate: Requires a standard factor panel (value/momentum/quality/etc.) plus a news feed; generate LLM embeddings of newsflow, combine with factor scores in a joint prediction model (e.g., gradient boosting or a small neural net), compare combined vs. factor-only vs. news-only performance.
notes: Directly relevant design pattern for a Massive-data-based book: combining a classic multi-factor panel with LLM-derived news embeddings is likely to be one of the more promising near-term directions given the broader literature's finding that text adds incremental (non-redundant) information over numeric factors alone.

title: Large Language Models and Futures Price Factors in China
authors: Yuhan Cheng, Heyang Zhou, Yanchu Liu
strategy: Uses LLMs (GPT-class models) to construct pricing factors for Chinese commodity/financial futures markets, an application of the LLM-factor-mining paradigm outside single-name equities.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning for Stock Returns
strategy: Concept-bottleneck deep-learning framework that forces the model to route through human-interpretable intermediate 'concepts' (synthesized predictors) before producing a cross-sectional return forecast, aiming to combine deep-learning power with interpretability, particularly for long-horizon predictions.
how_to_recreate: Requires a firm-characteristics panel; implement a concept-bottleneck architecture (characteristics -> interpretable concept layer -> return forecast), compare long-horizon (e.g., 1-year) return prediction R2/decile spread vs. a standard black-box neural net.
notes: Interpretability-focused variant of Gu-Kelly-Xiu-style ML prediction; exact performance numbers not retrieved in this pass.

title: On Evaluating Loss Functions for Stock Ranking: An Empirical Analysis With Transformer Model
strategy: Empirically compares different loss functions (pointwise regression vs. pairwise/listwise ranking losses) for training a transformer to rank stocks cross-sectionally, relevant to portfolio-construction-oriented (rather than pure return-forecast) model training.
how_to_recreate: Requires a firm-characteristics/price panel; train the same transformer architecture under different loss functions (MSE, pairwise ranking loss, listwise loss like ListMLE), compare resulting long-short portfolio performance.
notes: Useful methodological reference for how loss-function choice (not just architecture) affects the practical long-short performance of an ML stock-ranking model.

title: Gradient Boosting Decision Tree with LSTM for Investment Prediction

title: Quantpedia: aggregated ETF/momentum composite strategy backtest
strategy: Combines three momentum-style 'legs' into a single composite long-short strategy, selectively going long top-performing ETFs while shorting a small number of the weakest.
universe_period: Global ETFs (asset classes), period not fully specified

how_to_recreate: Requires only daily ETF prices across asset classes (equity, bond, commodity, currency ETFs); compute momentum ranks per leg, combine into a composite score, go long top ETFs / short bottom ETF(s), rebalance monthly; the strategy is invested less than half the days each month (partial time-in-market by design).
notes: A modest absolute Sharpe (0.55) reflects that this is a diversifying, low-turnover overlay rather than a high-conviction alpha strategy; more relevant to asset-allocation books than a tech-equity long/short book.

title: Winners vs. Losers: Momentum-Based Strategies with Intertemporal Choice for ESG Portfolios
strategy: Introduces a state-dependent momentum framework integrating ESG regime-switching with tail-risk-aware reward-risk metrics across three asset universes including the Russell 3000, examining whether policy/ESG sentiment drives cross-sectional return continuation.
how_to_recreate: Requires standard momentum signal construction plus an ESG-regime classification (e.g., based on ESG-related news flow/policy sentiment) and a tail-risk-aware position-sizing rule (similar in spirit to Daniel-Moskowitz dynamic scaling).
notes: Title/abstract only for detailed numbers; relevant if the target book incorporates ESG/policy-sentiment tilts alongside momentum.

title: Why Does Options Market Information Predict Stock Returns?
strategy: Tests whether the well-known predictive power of options-implied signals (volatility spread/skew) for equity returns survives once accounting for stock borrow fees; argues implied-vol signals largely proxy for the same informed-shorting information captured directly by borrow fees.
reported_return: once stock borrow fees are accounted for, strategies exploiting options-market-implied signals via short selling are 'much closer to break-even'
how_to_recreate: Requires options data (implied vols by strike/maturity, put-call skew) plus stock borrow-fee data. Compute standard vol-spread/skew factor, form long-short portfolio, then recompute net of realized borrow fee for the short leg.
notes: Directly ties the options-implied and short-interest literatures together; important caveat for any options-skew signal used in a long/short book -- gross backtest Sharpe from skew/vol-spread signals likely overstates net-of-borrow-cost performance.

strategy: Hierarchical RL portfolio-optimization framework: base RL agents process hybrid price+sentiment data per asset, meta-agents aggregate decisions across base agents, and a super-agent merges everything into final portfolio weights; sentiment comes from a lightweight LLM rather than a heavy full-scale model.

title: Risk-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Portfolio Optimization
strategy: PPO-based DRL portfolio optimizer with a Sharpe-ratio-based reward plus explicit risk controls (max-drawdown and volatility constraints) layered on top of the RL policy.

notes: Notably, the paper's own finding is negative/cautionary: the DRL agent stabilizes volatility but suffers degraded risk-adjusted returns due to over-conservative policy convergence -- a useful counter-example to more optimistic RL-portfolio papers on this list.

title: Anomalies and Their Short-Sale Costs
authors: Dmitriy Muravyev, Neil D. Pearson, Joshua M. Pollet
strategy: Re-tests 162 published cross-sectional anomalies after adjusting the short leg's return for actual stock-borrow (loan) fees rather than assuming free shorting.
universe_period: US equities, borrow-fee data 2006-2019 (or similar; anomaly universe per original papers)
reported_return: average long-short anomaly return is 0.14% per month before short-sale costs, but only -0.01% per month once adjusted for stock borrow fees; profits vanish even before fees if the ~12% of high-borrow-fee stock-days are excluded
how_to_recreate: Requires published anomaly signals (value, momentum, quality, etc.) plus a stock-borrow-fee/loan-fee dataset (e.g., from a securities-lending data vendor). Compute standard long-short anomaly returns, then re-compute the short leg's realized return net of the contemporaneous borrow fee for each name/day.
notes: Critical caveat paper for the entire anomaly literature: most published 'gross' long-short anomaly returns are not actually capturable once realistic borrow costs are included, especially in the crowded, hard-to-borrow small-cap short tail. Directly relevant to any long/short tech book -- shorting expensive-to-borrow names (e.g., heavily shorted momentum/growth names) can erase the anomaly's apparent edge.

title: A New Quality Factor Adjusted by Fraud Probability
authors: Ying Chen, Yuqiao Bu, Libing Fang, Yuanchu Xu
strategy: Modifies the standard Quality-Minus-Junk factor by down-weighting/excluding firms with a high estimated probability of financial-statement fraud (via a bivariate probit model that accounts for undetected fraud), producing a 'fraud-mitigated QMJ' (fmQMJ) factor.
reported_return: fmQMJ portfolio earns significant average excess returns in both China and the US, and outperforms the original QMJ factor specifically within low-size and low-book-to-market subgroups
how_to_recreate: Requires fundamentals plus a fraud-probability model (e.g., an F-score/M-score-style probit or logit model estimated on known historical fraud cases, extended with a bivariate specification for undetected fraud); compute standard QMJ, then re-weight/exclude high-fraud-probability names before forming the long-short portfolio.
notes: Directly relevant caution for small-cap/low-B/M value-quality strategies (exactly where accounting fraud risk concentrates); a fraud-probability overlay is a reasonable, implementable robustness layer on top of any fundamentals-based quality/value screen if audit/litigation/restatement data is available.

title: RiskMiner: Discovering Formulaic Alphas via Risk-Seeking Monte Carlo Tree Search
authors: Tao Ren, Ruihan Zhou, Jinyang Jiang, Jiafeng Liang, Qinghao Wang, Yijie Peng
strategy: Formulates formulaic-alpha mining as a reward-dense Markov Decision Process and solves it with a risk-seeking Monte Carlo Tree Search, aiming for alphas that are profitable under realistic backtesting rather than just high in-sample IC.

title: Reversals and the Returns to Liquidity Provision
authors: Wei Dai, Mamdouh Medhat, Robert Novy-Marx, Savina Rizova

notes: Reframes the classic short-term-reversal anomaly as compensation for bearing inventory risk as a liquidity provider -- implies realistic implementation must account for the same market-making costs (bid-ask spread, adverse selection) that generate the 'anomaly' in the first place, so gross backtest returns likely substantially overstate net edge for an outside participant.

notes: Popular open-source multi-agent trading framework (widely forked); like most LLM-agent trading papers, backtest windows are short and cost/capacity treatment is not rigorously disclosed in the abstract.

title: Sentiment Trading with Large Language Models

how_to_recreate: Needs a large historical news-article corpus timestamped to publication plus daily prices. Score each article's sentiment with an LLM, aggregate to a daily per-stock score, sort into long-short deciles, rebalance daily/next-day-open. Feasible with a Massive-style news feed plus any off-the-shelf or fine-tuned LLM/FinBERT.

Sharpe ratios this high for a pure sentiment factor should be treated with caution pending independent replication.

strategy: Distills classic Markowitz mean-variance optimization knowledge into a Bellman/RL-based portfolio policy, combining the interpretability of mean-variance theory with RL's ability to adapt dynamically.

how_to_recreate: Requires Dow-30-style multi-asset price history; implement a standard actor-critic or PPO DRL portfolio agent, benchmark cumulative return against buy-and-hold DJIA.

title: Statistical Arbitrage in Multi-Pair Trading Strategy Based on Graph Clustering Algorithms in US Equities Market
strategy: Uses graph-clustering algorithms (rather than pairwise correlation/cointegration search) to identify groups of related US equities for a multi-pair statistical-arbitrage strategy, trading mean-reversion within/between clusters.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily price/return data for a broad US equity universe; build a correlation/co-movement graph, cluster via a graph algorithm (e.g., Louvain community detection), form pairs/baskets within clusters, trade mean-reversion of the spread (z-score entry/exit rules), rebalance/rebuild clusters periodically.
notes: Directly implementable with daily prices alone (no fundamentals/news needed) -- one of the more turnkey stat-arb approaches on this list for a tech-heavy long/short book, since large tech/semis clusters are a natural fit for graph-based pair discovery.

title: Reinforcement Learning Pair Trading: A Dynamic Scaling Approach
strategy: RL agent learns to dynamically scale position size in a pairs-trading strategy (rather than using fixed z-score entry/exit thresholds), adapting exposure to the current spread regime.
how_to_recreate: Requires a cointegrated pair's spread history; train an RL agent (e.g., DQN/PPO) whose action is position size (not just binary long/short) as a function of the current spread z-score and recent spread volatility.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Advanced Statistical Arbitrage with Reinforcement Learning
strategy: General RL-based framework for statistical arbitrage, likely combining signal generation and execution/sizing within an RL policy.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily multi-asset price data; construct a stat-arb feature set (spreads, z-scores across candidate pairs/baskets), train an RL agent to trade the resulting mean-reversion signals.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Generating Synergistic Formulaic Alpha Collections via Reinforcement Learning (AlphaGen)
authors: Shuo Yu, Hongyan Xue, Xiang Ao, Feiyang Pan, Jia He, Dandan Tu, Qing He
strategy: Reinforcement-learning agent searches a formulaic-alpha expression space (combinations of price/volume operators) and is rewarded by the combined performance (IC) of the resulting alpha set rather than each alpha individually, producing a synergistic collection of low-correlation formulaic factors.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily OHLCV data and an operator library (rank, delay, correlation, ts_mean, etc.); define an RL environment where actions build alpha expression trees, reward = combined IC of the mined alpha set on a rolling training window, then backtest the mined factors via a standard factor-based long-short portfolio (e.g., top/bottom decile). Original codebase is public.
notes: Predecessor to RD-Agent(Q) and AlphaAgent; strong influence on the alpha-mining literature. Results are China A-share-specific (CSI300); direct transfer to US tech-heavy universe unverified. No explicit cost/capacity discussion found.

title: Earnings Forecasts and Revisions, Price Momentum, and Fundamental Data (chapter overview of AQR-style earnings-revision composites)
authors: John Guerard (chapter), summarizing decades of analyst-revision/EPS-momentum research including AQR fundamental-momentum composites
strategy: Composite of earnings momentum (trailing EPS growth), analyst estimate revisions (recent up/down revisions to consensus), and margin growth, combined with price momentum into a 'fundamental momentum' factor used by AQR and others; long stocks with positive revision momentum, short those with negative.
universe_period: US and global equities, multi-decade practitioner use
how_to_recreate: Requires consensus EPS estimate history (I/B/E/S-style, so revision direction/magnitude can be computed) plus prices. Compute 1-3 month change in consensus EPS estimate per stock, rank cross-sectionally, go long top revision decile / short bottom, rebalance monthly; smaller-cap names show a stronger effect per the underlying literature.
notes: This is a practitioner/survey-style anchor rather than a single rigorous academic paper with clean out-of-sample stats; useful mainly as a recipe (analyst-revision momentum is one of the more implementable, data-light factors if a fundamentals feed with consensus estimates is available).

title: PEAD.txt: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift Using Text
authors: Vitaly Meursault, Pierre Jinghong Liang, Bryan Routledge, Madeline Marco Scanlon
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
strategy: Defines earnings surprise using a text-based measure derived from earnings-call transcripts/press releases (rather than the standard analyst-consensus EPS surprise), and shows a long-short PEAD strategy sorted on this text-based surprise produces stronger post-earnings drift than surprise-based on numbers alone.
reported_return: text-based PEAD strategy generates drift of about 1.11%-2.87% over the post-announcement window (varies by exact text specification), versus smaller drift (~1.65%) from alternative text/quintile-spread measures
how_to_recreate: Requires earnings-call transcripts or press releases plus standard EPS-surprise data and post-announcement daily returns. Construct a text-based surprise score (e.g., via a trained classifier or embedding similarity to prior calls), sort firms into deciles at announcement, hold 20-60 trading days, rebalance each earnings season.
notes: A foundational text-based-PEAD paper feeding much of the later LLM-earnings-call literature; drift is measured gross of costs and pre-dates modern LLM embeddings, so a Massive-style news+transcript feed with an LLM embedding could likely reproduce or extend it.

title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design
strategy: Single-stock LLM trading agent with a layered memory system (working memory plus long-term memory with different retention horizons) and a configurable 'risk character,' used to summarize multi-source information (news, prices, fundamentals) into trading decisions.
universe_period: Individual stocks, backtest period not fully captured
reported_sharpe: reported to significantly outperform other LLM trading agents on cumulative return and Sharpe ratio in its own comparisons
how_to_recreate: Requires news + price + fundamentals per stock; implement a layered memory buffer (short-term 'working memory' plus decaying long-term memory) feeding an LLM decision prompt each day, with a configurable risk-aversion parameter.
notes: One of the earliest and most-cited 'LLM agent with memory' trading papers (late 2023); single-stock backtests of this era are widely noted to be short-horizon and susceptible to hindsight/overfitting in agent prompt design.

title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance
strategy: Debate-driven multi-agent LLM trading system where agents with distinct 'characters'/risk profiles debate a trading decision, aiming to improve sentiment classification robustness and reduce single-agent hallucination/bias.
how_to_recreate: Similar recreation pattern to TradingAgents/FinMem: multiple LLM personas debate, an aggregator agent decides.
notes: Title/abstract only; grouped with FinMem/TradingAgents as an early multi-agent LLM trading paper.

title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models
strategy: Feed news headlines to GPT and other LLMs, prompting a good/bad/unclear sentiment classification for the stock's price; aggregate into a numeric daily 'ChatGPT score' per stock and go long high-score / short low-score names.
universe_period: US equities, news headlines through 2023 (with a post-training-cutoff subsample used as an out-of-sample test)
how_to_recreate: Needs a timestamped news-headline feed plus daily prices. Prompt an LLM per headline for a -1/0/+1 sentiment score, aggregate scores per stock per day, form daily long-short decile portfolios on the score, hold 1 day (or a few days for the drift component). Directly implementable with a Massive-style news+price feed.
notes: Landmark paper showing LLM sentiment has real short-horizon predictive power, but by the authors' own account, publicizing the signal erodes it ('returns decline as adoption rises') — a live LLM-based headline strategy in 2026 should expect materially decayed edge versus 2023 figures. No cost-adjustment; hit-rate/day, not $ return.

title: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing
authors: Luyang Chen, Markus Pelger, Jason Zhu
strategy: Conditional-autoencoder deep neural network estimates a nonlinear, time-varying asset pricing (SDF) model for individual stock returns using firm characteristics and macro conditioning variables, trained with a no-arbitrage / pricing-error objective and adversarially-constructed test portfolios.
universe_period: US equities, CRSP sample spanning multiple decades
reported_sharpe: outperforms benchmark factor models out-of-sample on Sharpe ratio of the mean-variance efficient factor portfolio, explained variation, and pricing errors (exact numeric Sharpe not captured in this pass)
how_to_recreate: Requires firm-characteristics panel + macro series + returns; implement a conditional autoencoder (characteristics -> latent factor loadings, and factors themselves estimated from returns) trained via a no-arbitrage loss. Feasible only with a rich fundamentals+macro dataset, not prices alone.
notes: Highly cited but methodologically complex; identifies price trend, liquidity and value as top firm characteristics driving the learned factors. Academic backtest, not live/cost-adjusted.

title: Spatio-Temporal Momentum: Jointly Learning Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Strategies
authors: Wee Ling Tan, Stephen Roberts, Stefan Zohren
venue: Journal of Financial Data Science / arXiv:2302.10175
strategy: A single neural network (even a simple one-layer network) is trained jointly across assets to produce both time-series and cross-sectional momentum signals simultaneously, sharing information across the cross-section instead of fitting per-asset models.
universe_period: 46 actively-traded US equities and 12 equity index futures
reported_sharpe: reported to retain performance advantage over single-asset TSMOM/cross-sectional benchmarks; exact Sharpe not captured in this pass
how_to_recreate: Daily prices for a modest cross-section (dozens of names) suffice; construct a pooled training set of lagged returns across assets, train one shared network to output per-asset positions, apply LASSO/turnover regularization, and test robustness at 5-10bps costs.
notes: Small universe (46 stocks) — capacity and generalization to broader US equity universes untested here.

title: Deep Inception Networks: A General End-to-End Framework for Multi-Asset Quantitative Strategies
strategy: Applies an Inception-style (multi-scale convolutional) deep-learning architecture end-to-end across multiple assets for quantitative trend/momentum-style strategies, aiming to capture patterns at multiple time scales simultaneously.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily multi-asset price history; build multi-scale convolutional feature extractors (parallel kernels at different lookback lengths) feeding a position-sizing output layer trained end-to-end (e.g., Sharpe-loss as in the DMN papers).
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass -- grouped with the broader deep-trend-following literature (DMN, Momentum Transformer).

title: Few-Shot Learning Patterns in Financial Time-Series for Trend-Following Strategies
strategy: Applies few-shot learning techniques to identify recurring price patterns useful for trend-following, aiming to adapt quickly to new instruments/regimes with limited data.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily price data across a broad instrument set for meta-training, then a few-shot fine-tuning step on a new/target instrument with limited history.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Constructing Time-Series Momentum Portfolios with Deep Multi-Task Learning
strategy: Uses a multi-task learning architecture (shared representation across related prediction tasks, e.g., multiple horizons or multiple instruments) to construct time-series momentum portfolios.
how_to_recreate: Requires multi-asset daily price data; define related auxiliary tasks (e.g., predicting returns at multiple horizons, or across related instruments) trained jointly with a shared encoder, use the shared representation to size TSMOM positions.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Cross-Sectional Variation of Option-Implied Volatility Skew
strategy: Documents systematic cross-sectional variation in equity option-implied volatility skew (OTM put IV minus ATM call IV) and links it to expected stock returns and firm characteristics.
how_to_recreate: Requires listed-options implied-vol surfaces by underlying/date; compute the OTM-put-vs-ATM-call skew per name per day, sort into deciles, form a long-short equity portfolio (short high negative skew / long low skew, or vice versa per the paper's sign convention), rebalance monthly.
notes: Seminal-ish anchor for the options-skew-predicts-returns literature; see Muravyev et al. and the JFE 2025 paper above for the borrow-fee counter-evidence.

title: Select and Trade: Towards Unified Pair Trading with Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
strategy: Hierarchical RL framework that jointly handles pair selection (which stocks to pair) and trade execution (when/how much to trade the spread) in a single unified pipeline, rather than treating selection and trading as separate stages.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily price history for a broad equity universe; a high-level RL policy selects candidate pairs (from correlation/cointegration/co-movement features), a low-level RL policy executes the spread-trading decision, trained jointly or in alternation.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
authors: Yukun Liu, Aleh Tsyvinski, Xi Wu
strategy: Constructs cryptocurrency counterparts of standard equity return predictors and shows that a three-factor model (crypto market, crypto size, crypto momentum) captures most of the cross-sectional variation in expected cryptocurrency returns; ten crypto characteristics form significant long-short strategies largely spanned by this C-3 model.
universe_period: Broad cryptocurrency universe, sample spanning roughly 2014-2018
how_to_recreate: Requires daily crypto price/volume/market-cap history across a broad coin universe. Compute crypto-market excess return, crypto-size (small-minus-big market cap) and crypto-momentum (trailing-return-sorted) factors; form and backtest additional long-short characteristic portfolios, test whether the C-3 model spans them via time-series regression.
notes: Seminal anchor for crypto factor investing; standard equity factor models (FF3/Carhart4/FF5) do not explain crypto cross-sectional returns, motivating crypto-specific factors. Gross of costs; crypto exchange/borrow costs and extreme volatility materially affect implementability.

title: Is Factor Momentum More than Stock Momentum?
venue: Journal of Finance (working paper version arXiv:2009.04824)
strategy: Shows that momentum in factor returns themselves (buying factors that have recently done well, shorting those that have done poorly) explains most forms of individual-stock momentum (standard momentum, industry momentum, industry-adjusted momentum), suggesting stock momentum is largely 'factor momentum in disguise.'
universe_period: US equity factor portfolios, multi-decade sample
how_to_recreate: Requires a broad panel of factor return series (dozens of published anomaly/factor portfolios); compute each factor's own trailing momentum, form a factor-momentum long-short portfolio (long recently-winning factors, short recently-losing factors), compare its explanatory power for stock-level momentum via spanning regressions.
notes: Influential but debated -- later work (2024-2025, e.g., Quoniam's 'Many Facets of Stock Momentum') finds factor momentum does not fully explain price/industry momentum internationally, suggesting the original US result may not generalize cleanly.

title: They Still Haven't Told You: An Analysis of the Overnight/Intraday Anomaly's Robustness
strategy: Further scrutiny of the overnight/intraday return decomposition, examining robustness/explanations for why overnight returns dominate cumulative equity performance.
how_to_recreate: Same OHLC-only recreation as the overnight/intraday papers above.
notes: Title/abstract only; included for category completeness.

title: Detecting Data-Driven Robust Statistical Arbitrage Strategies with Deep Neural Networks
strategy: Uses a deep neural network to identify robust statistical-arbitrage strategies across multiple securities simultaneously, without requiring explicit pairwise cointegration testing.
how_to_recreate: Requires multi-asset daily price history; train a neural network to directly output a statistical-arbitrage trading strategy (portfolio weights over time) optimized for a robust arbitrage-style objective, rather than first testing pairwise cointegration.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Trading with the Momentum Transformer: An Intelligent and Interpretable Architecture
authors: Kieran Wood, Stephen Roberts, Stefan Zohren
strategy: Attention-based transformer trend-following model with an added change-point detection (CPD) module that flags regime shifts, feeding into position sizing; outputs positions directly (Sharpe-optimized) rather than return forecasts.
reported_sharpe: adding CPD module improves Sharpe ratio by about one-third over 1995-2020, and by about two-thirds over the more recent 2015-2020 subperiod, net of transaction costs
how_to_recreate: Continuous daily futures data; build change-point-detection features (Gaussian process based) plus price/volatility features; train transformer with attention over lookback window, Sharpe-ratio loss, walk-forward retraining across regimes (including COVID).
notes: Improvement is measured against the authors' own DMN/TSMOM baselines, not against a simple buy-and-hold; capacity and crowding for futures trend-followers are separate concerns not addressed here.

title: Trend-Following Strategies via Dynamic Momentum Learning
authors: Bruno P. C. Levy et al.
strategy: Learns a dynamic (time-varying) momentum lookback/weighting scheme rather than a fixed lookback window, adapting trend-following signal construction to changing market dynamics.
how_to_recreate: Requires daily multi-asset price data; replace the fixed-lookback trend signal with a learned, time-varying weighting function over past returns (e.g., via a small neural net or attention layer), train to maximize a Sharpe-like objective.
notes: Title/abstract only; not independently verified in this pass.

title: Value Investing Research: Simple Methods to Improve the Piotroski F-Score
authors: Alpha Architect research team (practitioner research building on Piotroski 2000)
strategy: Tests simple modifications to Piotroski's original 9-signal F-Score (profitability, leverage/liquidity, operating efficiency binary signals) to improve its ability to separate future winners from losers among cheap (high book-to-market) value stocks.
how_to_recreate: Requires standard fundamentals (ROA, change in ROA, CFO, CFO vs. net income, change in leverage, change in current ratio, share issuance, change in gross margin, change in asset turnover); compute the 9 binary signals, sum to a 0-9 F-Score, apply within a cheap-valuation (high B/M) universe, long high F-Score / short or avoid low F-Score.
notes: F-Score is one of the cheapest-to-implement fundamental composites (needs only standard financial-statement line items, no text/news); best used as a quality overlay on a value screen rather than standalone, per the original Piotroski (2000) design, which is itself the seminal anchor for this factor family.

title: Strikingly Suspicious Overnight and Intraday Returns
strategy: Documents that a large, often near-monotonic fraction of long-run US equity index (and many single-stock) returns is earned overnight (close-to-open) rather than intraday (open-to-close), and questions the stability/causes of this pattern.
reported_return: over a recent 5-year window (Q3 2020-Q3 2025, per secondary sources), SPY close-to-open return was about +47.1% vs. +29.9% open-to-close; QQQ close-to-open was about +53.5% vs. +30.3% open-to-close
how_to_recreate: Only needs daily open/close/prior-close prices (no fundamentals or text). Compute close-to-open and open-to-close return series per name/index, compare cumulative performance, and construct a strategy that holds overnight and is flat/hedged intraday (or the reverse) to isolate the effect.
notes: One of the most directly and cheaply implementable anomalies on this list (needs only OHLC prices), but it is extremely well known and crowded by 2026; net-of-cost edge for a pure overnight-hold strategy on liquid large-caps is likely thin given borrow/financing costs of holding overnight and the well-documented decay of such 'anomalies' once publicized.

title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
authors: Shihao Gu, Bryan Kelly, Dacheng Xiu
strategy: Compares linear, penalized linear, PCR/PLS, boosted trees, random forests and neural networks for predicting individual US stock returns from ~900 firm-characteristic/macro interaction predictors; builds long-short decile portfolios sorted on each model's fitted return.
how_to_recreate: Needs a broad firm-characteristics panel (~94 characteristics x macro interactions) plus monthly returns (e.g., CRSP + Compustat equivalent, or a proprietary fundamentals+prices feed like Massive). Standard pipeline: expanding-window training, refit annually, rank-sort predicted returns into deciles, long top/short bottom.
notes: Landmark ML-in-finance paper; R2 numbers are tiny in absolute terms (predictability is real but weak) — long-short portfolio Sharpe gains come from ranking, not point-forecast accuracy. Gross of costs.

title: Enhancing Time-Series Momentum Strategies Using Deep Neural Networks (Deep Momentum Networks)
authors: Bryan Lim, Stefan Zohren, Stephen Roberts
venue: arXiv / Journal of Financial Data Science
strategy: Deep Momentum Networks: an LSTM directly outputs a trading-rule position (not just a return forecast) that is trained end-to-end to maximize a differentiable Sharpe-ratio objective, replacing hand-crafted trend/vol-scaling rules.
universe_period: 88 continuous futures contracts across asset classes, ~1990-2015
reported_sharpe: Sharpe-optimized LSTM improves on traditional TSMOM by more than 2x gross of costs; still outperforms with 2-3bps transaction costs
how_to_recreate: Requires continuous daily futures price series (~88 contracts) and engineered features (returns/vol at multiple lookbacks, MACD-style indicators). Train an LSTM per instrument or pooled, with a differentiable Sharpe loss; walk-forward retrain and combine positions with vol targeting.
notes: One of the most-cited deep-learning trend-following papers; basis for the later Momentum Transformer. Reported outperformance narrows sharply once realistic costs and capacity constraints are included.

title: The Loan Fee Anomaly: A Short Seller's Best Ideas
authors: Adam Reed, Matthew Ringgenberg (or related; cited via SSRN and paperswithbacktest summary)
strategy: Stocks with high (and rising) stock-loan/borrow fees are shorted by informed short sellers ('best ideas'); sorting stocks by borrow fee alone produces a stronger long-short return than sorting by 102 traditional anomaly signals.
reported_return: portfolios formed on borrow fees provide larger long-short returns than portfolios formed on any of 102 compared anomalies over 2006-2019
how_to_recreate: Requires a securities-lending/borrow-fee data feed by stock and date. Rank stocks by borrow fee level (and/or fee changes), short high-fee names, long low-fee names, rebalance monthly.
notes: Because the strategy's own edge is proportional to borrow fee, the strategy is inherently expensive to implement at scale on the short side -- the 'anomaly' partly reflects the informed-shorting signal, not a free lunch; overlaps conceptually with the Muravyev et al. (2025) short-sale-cost paper above.

title: Quality Minus Junk
authors: Clifford S. Asness, Andrea Frazzini, Lasse H. Pedersen
venue: Review of Accounting Studies (working paper circulated 2013+)
strategy: Blends multiple quality sub-scores -- profitability, growth, safety (low leverage/low earnings volatility/low beta), and payout/management quality -- into a single composite Quality-Minus-Junk (QMJ) factor; long high-quality stocks, short low-quality ('junk'), often combined with value.
universe_period: US and international equities, multi-decade sample (1957-2016 in later AQR data updates)
how_to_recreate: Requires fundamentals (profitability ratios, leverage, earnings/ROE volatility, payout ratio) plus price-derived beta; z-score and average the four quality sub-components per firm, rank cross-sectionally, go long top quality decile / short bottom, rebalance monthly-to-quarterly. AQR publishes a monthly QMJ factor return series for direct benchmarking.
notes: One of the most widely used quality composites in practice; AQR provides the constructed factor series publicly for validation. Gross of costs, published construction may already be crowded/lower-Sharpe out of the original sample.

title: Momentum Crashes
strategy: Documents that momentum strategies occasionally suffer large, persistent crashes (notably 2009), concentrated in past-loser portfolios during market rebounds following high-volatility periods, and proposes dynamically scaling momentum exposure by forecasted variance/market-state to avoid crash periods.
how_to_recreate: Requires only daily/monthly prices. Construct standard 12-month momentum long-short portfolio, compute rolling realized market volatility, scale gross momentum exposure down (or hedge the short-loser leg) when past volatility is high and the market has recently been down (bear-market-rebound risk state), rebalance monthly.
notes: Seminal anchor for momentum crash risk and dynamic risk-managed momentum; directly relevant to any momentum sleeve in a tech-heavy book, since past-loser short legs are exactly where crash risk concentrates during sharp market rebounds (e.g., post-drawdown tech rallies).

title: Betting Against Beta
strategy: Constructs a leverage-adjusted, beta-neutral long-short portfolio: long low-beta stocks (levered up to unit beta), short high-beta stocks (delevered to unit beta), designed to exploit leverage-constrained investors' tendency to overweight high-beta stocks and thus underprice low-beta ones.
universe_period: US and 19 other international equity markets, plus Treasury bonds, credit and futures, multi-decade sample
how_to_recreate: Requires only prices (to estimate rolling betas) -- no fundamentals needed. Estimate each stock's rolling beta (e.g., 1-year daily or 5-year monthly), rank into low/high-beta portfolios, weight to be beta-neutral overall (lever the low-beta leg, delever the high-beta leg), rebalance monthly.
notes: Original paper reports the strategy's return 'rivals those of all the standard asset pricing factors...in terms of economic magnitude, statistical significance and robustness,' per author framing -- but subsequent literature (e.g., 'Betting Against Betting Against Beta,' 'The Volatility Puzzle of the Beta Anomaly,' 2025) has challenged both the magnitude and the leverage-constraint explanation. Gross of costs; gross-leverage assumptions (using leverage to reach unit beta) are not costless in practice (financing/margin costs).

title: The Gross Profitability Premium
strategy: Sorts stocks on gross profitability (revenue minus cost of goods sold, scaled by total assets) as a cleaner, less-manipulable profitability/quality measure than net income; long high gross-profitability stocks, short low, often combined with a value tilt ('the other side of value').
reported_return: profitable-minus-unprofitable long-short spread has a Fama-French-3-factor alpha of about 0.52% per month (t-stat 4.49); a 2015 international extension found an average annual profitability premium of about 3.6% across 15 European markets, 1982-2014
how_to_recreate: Only needs fundamentals (revenue, COGS, total assets) plus prices -- no text/news required. Compute gross profitability = (Revenue - COGS) / Total Assets per firm per fiscal year, rank cross-sectionally at each rebalance (typically annual, aligned to fiscal-year-end + reporting lag), go long top decile / short bottom decile, hold ~1 year (or blend with a monthly price-based tilt).
notes: Seminal quality/profitability anchor; combines well with value (low P/B, high gross profitability = 'quality value'). Gross of costs, largely in-sample discovery period; profitability premium has been shown to decay/compress post-publication like most anomalies.

title: Time Series Momentum
authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse H. Pedersen
strategy: For each of 58 futures/forwards (equities, bonds, currencies, commodities), go long if trailing 12-month excess return is positive, short if negative; volatility-scale each position and combine into a diversified portfolio.
universe_period: 58 liquid futures/forward contracts across asset classes, 1985-2009
reported_return: positive time-series momentum return for essentially every contract; diversified TSMOM portfolio Sharpe reported well above 1
reported_sharpe: diversified portfolio Sharpe ratio > 1 (exact figure not captured from this pass)
how_to_recreate: Needs daily futures/continuous-contract prices (equities alone insufficient for full replication, but the sign-of-trailing-return + vol-scaling rule can be applied to any daily price series, including single-name equities or sector ETFs). Rebalance monthly.
notes: Seminal anchor for time-series momentum / trend-following; in-sample period, gross of costs. Basis for most modern deep-learning TSMOM papers below.

title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings? (the accrual anomaly)
strategy: Sorts stocks on the accrual component of earnings (earnings minus operating cash flow, scaled by assets); long low-accrual (cash-flow-backed earnings) stocks, short high-accrual (earnings management-prone) stocks, based on evidence that the market underreacts to the lower persistence of accruals vs. cash flows.
universe_period: US equities, 1962-1991 (original); a 1972-2010 replication finds similar magnitude
reported_return: a low-minus-high total-accruals long-short portfolio earns a significant average return of about 0.71% per month (~8.5% annualized) in a 1972-2010 replication
how_to_recreate: Only needs fundamentals (net income, cash flow from operations, total assets) -- no prices needed for signal construction. Compute accruals = (Net Income - CFO) / Total Assets per firm-year, rank cross-sectionally at fiscal-year-end (with reporting lag), go long low-accrual decile / short high-accrual decile, hold ~1 year, rebalance annually.
notes: Classic anchor anomaly; closely related to and partially subsumed by gross-profitability/quality factors in later literature (accruals and R&D both sit in the 'earnings vs. gross-profit wedge'). Gross of costs; well-documented decay since publication.

title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
strategy: Rank US stocks on trailing 3-12 month returns; go long past winners and short past losers, holding 3-12 months, skipping a short formation-to-holding gap.
reported_return: approx. 1% per month (about 12% annualized) for 6-month formation/6-month holding long-short
how_to_recreate: Daily/monthly close prices only. Compute trailing J-month cumulative return per stock, sort into deciles, go long top decile / short bottom decile, hold K months with monthly overlapping rebalancing. Fully doable with daily price history alone.
notes: Seminal anchor paper for cross-sectional momentum; in-sample discovery period, no transaction costs. Momentum crashes (2009) and post-2000s decay are well documented in follow-on literature.
